title: Data Structures in Java
syllabus: Week 1-2 Java review, classes and interfaces. Week 3-4 Linked lists and iterators. Week 5 Stacks and queues. Week 6 Recursion. Week 7 Midterm. Week 8-9 Binary search trees. Week 10 Hash tables. Week 11 Heaps and priority queues. Week 12-13 Sorting (insertion, merge, quick) and searching. Week 14 Big-O analysis. Week 15 Final project. Assessment: 6 programming assignments 40%, midterm 25%, final 35%. Contact hours: 3 lecture + 2 lab per week. Textbook: Data Structures and Abstractions with Java.

title: Research Methods in the Behavioral Sciences
syllabus: Week 1 Science and psychology. Week 2 Ethics and IRB. Week 3 Measurement, reliability and validity. Week 4 Survey and correlational designs. Week 5-6 Experimental designs, control and confounds. Week 7 Midterm. Week 8 Descriptive statistics. Week 9 t-tests. Week 10 Intro to ANOVA (one-way only). Week 11-13 Class lab experiment: design, data collection, analysis. Week 14 APA-style writing. Week 15 Final paper. Assessment: lab report 35%, exams 40%, homework 25%. Contact hours: 3 lecture + 1 lab per week.

title: Linear Algebra
syllabus: 10-week quarter. Wk 1 Linear systems and row reduction. Wk 2 Matrix algebra. Wk 3 Inverses and LU. Wk 4 Determinants. Wk 5 Midterm; vector spaces. Wk 6 Subspaces, basis, dimension. Wk 7 Linear transformations. Wk 8 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Wk 9 Diagonalisation, orthogonality. Wk 10 Least squares, review. Assessment: weekly homework 20%, midterm 30%, final 50%. Contact: 4 lecture hours/week.

title: Program Design and Implementation 1
syllabus: OOP in Java: classes, interfaces, inheritance, polymorphism, generics, unit testing, abstraction, simple design patterns. Lab weekly. Data structures (trees, hashing, heaps) are deferred to CS 2700.

title: Statistics for the Behavioral Sciences
syllabus: Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling distributions, z and t tests, one- and two-way ANOVA, correlation and regression, nonparametric tests. Problem sets in R. No lab and no research project.

title: Introduction to Econometrics
syllabus: Wk 1-2 Review of probability and statistics. Wk 3-5 Simple and multiple OLS regression. Wk 6 Midterm. Wk 7 Heteroskedasticity and specification. Wk 8 Binary dependent variables. Wk 9 Instrumental variables (introduction). Wk 10 Applied project presentations. Software: Stata.
